stemBlocks.value: A, B, C and D lie on a circle with centre O. AOC and BOD are diameters, and AB is parallel to DC. On the diagram angle BAC = 2p°, angle BCA = 3p°, angle BDC = q° and angle ACD = r°. (i) State why angle ABC = 90°. (ii) Determine, with reasons, (a) angle BAC and (b) angle q. (iii) Calculate the value of angle r.
Think first: AC is a diameter, so the angle at B is 90° — that turns the two algebraic angles into a simple equation.

solutionSteps.instruction: Explain the right angle at B.

contentBlocks.value: AOC is a diameter and B is on the circumference, so ∠ABC stands on a semicircle

solutionSteps.instruction: Write the angle sum of triangle ABC in terms of p.
Solve for p and hence for angle BAC.

contentBlocks.value: Both angles stand on chord BC and both lie in the same segment

solutionSteps.instruction: Use the parallel lines AB and DC with transversal AC.

contentBlocks.value: ∠BAC and ∠ACD are alternate angles between the parallel lines

strategyBlocks.value: Use the right angle at B to solve 2p + 3p + 90 = 180 for p, then get q as an angle in the same segment as ∠BAC and r as an alternate angle to ∠BAC across the parallel lines.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: (i) ∠ABC = 90° because it is the angle in a semicircle — AOC is a diameter.  (ii) a) ∠BAC = 36° (from 2p + 3p + 90 = 180, so p = 18)  b) q = 36° — angles in the same segment, standing on chord BC, are equal.  (iii) r = 36° — alternate angles, since AB is parallel to DC and AC is a transversal.

whyThisWorks.value: The angle in a semicircle is 90° because the diameter subtends a straight angle of 180° at the centre and the angle at the circumference is half of it. That fixed 90° leaves only 90° for the two algebraic angles, which is what makes p solvable. The same-segment rule then transfers ∠BAC to D without any new calculation, and the parallel lines transfer it again to r — one 36° angle appears three times in the figure.
